name: Mphasis
summary: Mphasis is known for its work with banking, capital markets and insurance clients, and its interviews often reflect that domain. Candidates commonly report an online assessment for fresher drives, technical interviews on fundamentals, coding and their projects, and an HR round. It publishes five cultural principles, including 'Ready, fire, aim' and 'Disagree but Commit', which make useful material for behavioural answers.
rounds: Campus drive, online application or referral
Online assessment for many fresher drives: aptitude, English and coding
Technical interview on fundamentals, coding and your projects
For experienced roles: a second technical or managerial round
looks_for: Interest in banking and insurance technology for many roles
Clear communication with clients and teammates

covers: Your degree or experience and the technologies you know best
One project with your part in it and a result
Why this role, in under two minutes

questions.text: Tell me about a time you tried something quickly, it didn't work, and you learned from it.
covers: What you tried and why speed mattered more than a perfect plan
How you found out it didn't work
What you changed and what the second attempt achieved

questions.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision but committed to it once it was made.
covers: Your view and the decision that went the other way
How you made your case, respectfully and with reasons
How you then backed the decision fully, and what happened

questions.text: Tell me about a time you stepped outside your role to help your team get something done.
covers: What was at risk and why you stepped in
What you did that wasn't in your job description
The result for the team

questions.text: What's a skill you've had to work hard to improve, and how are you doing it?
covers: The skill and why it didn't come easily
Your plan: practice, feedback, courses
The progress you can show so far

questions.text: What is a database transaction, and what do the ACID properties mean?
covers: A group of steps that succeed or fail together, such as a money transfer
Atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability: one line each
What goes wrong without them, for example money debited but not credited

questions.text: How would you design the tables for a simple bank account system with deposits and withdrawals?
covers: Tables for customers, accounts and transactions, with keys
Storing each transaction rather than only overwriting the balance
Rules such as no overdraft, and how you'd keep balances correct

questions.text: What is the difference between authentication and authorisation? Use a banking app as the example.
covers: Authentication checks who you are: password, OTP, biometrics
Authorisation checks what you're allowed to do: view, transfer, approve
Why both matter, and a mistake that would expose data

questions.text: Explain exception handling in your language, and what you'd log when a payment fails.
covers: Try, catch and finally (or the equivalent), and when to rethrow
Logging useful context, such as a transaction ID and error code, but never card or password data
Showing the user a clear message and leaving the system in a safe state

questions.text: Two withdrawals hit the same account at the same moment. What could go wrong, and how would you prevent it?
covers: The race: both read the old balance and the account goes below zero
Fixes: database transactions with locks, or a check-and-update in one step
How you'd test for it

questions.text: For experienced candidates: tell me about a legacy system you worked on and how you changed it safely.
covers: What the system did and why changing it was risky
How you protected it: tests first, small steps, feature flags or parallel runs
What you changed and how you knew nothing broke
Something specific: its work in banking or insurance, or its cultural principles
How that fits your skills or interests
What you'd like to learn there

questions.text: Would you be happy to work in financial-services domains such as banking or insurance? Why?
covers: An honest answer and what interests you about the domain
Anything you already know, such as how payments or claims work
How you'd learn the domain quickly

questions.text: What would you want to learn in your first year here?
covers: One or two concrete skills linked to the role
How you'd learn them on the job and on your own
A question back about how new joiners are supported

tips: Revise database transactions, SQL and one language well; banking and insurance work leans on them.
Read Mphasis's five cultural principles and prepare a short example for 'Disagree but Commit' and 'Ready, fire, aim'.
Learn some basic banking and insurance words (account, transaction, settlement, policy, claim) so domain questions don't surprise you.
Be ready to explain one project end to end, including how you tested it.

rounds: Manager or client interview (for many roles)
